label: early original-phase input of f/p/1/h/d/x/i/m (steps 2-5)
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, never at the delimiter or during copy, and almost never at steps 0-1 or after step 6; it peaks at step 3 (42% of mass), with steps 2-4 holding about 91%. It is token-selective: f is the strongest and most frequent (30% rate, 27% of mass; top activations are nearly all f at step 3, often after i/d), followed by p, 1, h, d, then x, i, m. Rarely fires on s, u, 3 or r. It fires more on first occurrences of a token (89% of mass), but requiring in_first lowers recall more than it raises precision. Sequence length, digit count and later tokens barely matter. The predicate (steps 2-5, one of the 8 tokens) covers about 95% of activation mass on dev, but precision is only about 0.62: many matching steps stay below threshold, so magnitude also depends on the context of earlier tokens, which this predicate does not capture.
